elements.requirement: A person is not excused from answering any question put to them in proceedings for the recovery or administration of any property, for the execution of any trust, or for an account of any property or dealings with property on the ground that answering may incriminate that person or their spouse or civil partner of an offence under the Criminal Damage Act 1971.
elements.quote: A person shall not be excused, by reason that to do so may incriminate that person or the spouse or civil partner of that person of an offence under this Act— (a) from answering any question put to that person in proceedings for the recovery or administration of any property, for the execution of any trust or for an account of any property or dealings with property

elements.requirement: A person is not excused from complying with any order made in proceedings for the recovery or administration of property, the execution of a trust, or an account of property or dealings with property on the ground that complying may incriminate that person or their spouse or civil partner of an offence under the Criminal Damage Act 1971.
elements.quote: from complying with any order made in any such proceedings

elements.requirement: No statement or admission made by a person when answering such a question or complying with such an order is admissible in evidence against that person in proceedings for an offence under the Criminal Damage Act 1971.
elements.quote: no statement or admission made by a person in answering a question put or complying with an order made as aforesaid shall, in proceedings for an offence under this Act, be admissible in evidence against that person

elements.requirement: No statement or admission made by a person when answering such a question or complying with such an order is admissible in evidence against that person's spouse or civil partner in proceedings for an offence under the Criminal Damage Act 1971, unless they married or became civil partners after the statement or admission was made.
elements.quote: (unless they married or became civil partners after the making of the statement or admission) against the spouse or civil partner of that person
